name: 434. A vendor's own name for a price-affecting field is checked like the unified field (vendor-price-name)
description: Folder 430 pins that an extra param cannot supply a price-affecting unified field the request did not send. That rule compared the unified name only, so a converter that reads the vendor's own name for the same field still took a value no unified field showed: ratio on a Seedance or MiniMax video, aspectRatio on a Veo video, outputFormat on a Runware video. schemas.VendorPriceFieldNames now maps each such name, per provider and operation, to its unified field, and the request worker refuses it exactly as it refuses the unified name: 400 caller_unsupported_parameter naming the vendor's field, unless the request sent the unified field with the same value. A name is mapped only where the converter delivers the unified field, so the caller who is refused can send that instead; the BytePlus, MiniMax and Gemini video converters gained delivery of aspect_ratio for this. Go pins the table over every entry, a lint over the converters' source that fails when one reads an unlisted price-looking name, and every integration route's own ingress through the worker. These rows pin the refusal on the native routes, where an unknown top-level field or form field is an extra param: /v1/videos for the video names, /v1/audio/speech and /v1/audio/transcriptions for Sarvam's. Sarvam's speaker has no row of its own without a voice, because the speech route requires voice; it is refused there when it differs from the voice sent. The ten refusal rows are refused before any upstream call, so none creates a task. The next three rows pin the other half: the unified aspect_ratio, sent with a size that would derive 16:9, reaches BytePlus and MiniMax as ratio and Gemini as aspectRatio. An accepted video create is a billed task at a real vendor, so those three run only on the provider error fixture (providerErrorFixture=1), which answers each vendor's task shape and returns what it was sent from /__wire; elsewhere they are skipped. The last row is the genai route's own Veo request, with aspectRatio and resolution in parameters: the route carries them as the unified fields as well, so the worker accepts its own request, and they reach Veo unchanged. It runs on the fixture for the same reason.
